note: N5a. Every threshold of the world scheduler (kernel/world/tiers.gd). Distances are metres from the player to the nearest edge of a plot's footprint (0 = inside). A walk script may override any key under its own "tiers". kernel/world/TIERS.md says what each one does and what was measured.
backdrop_note: outer edge of backdrop; beyond it a pack goes to ledger (unloaded, summary only). 0 = no pack is unloaded for distance.
restart_note: N7, worlds with a visitor: a game that ended by itself and is not on stage starts its next round this many world ticks after it ended (or after the visitor left it). 0 = it stays over. OWNER, 2026-11-11: the idea is paused; how games start and how a player engages with them is a chapter of its own. Keep 0 until that chapter is designed.
slice_note: OWNER, 2026-11-11: a far game never runs slower than one sixteenth of real time (max 16). When the far tier needs more than that, the valve slows the whole world instead.
load_note: P5, the build queue (kernel/world/jobs.gd). mode: queue = a pack is prepared on a worker thread and attached at a tick boundary when it is ready, nearest first (a world somebody looks at); step = one pack per world tick in the same order, built whole on the main thread (the arrival tick is a pure function of the walk); wait = as step but prepared on the worker and waited for (tests of the worker's path); auto = queue in a window, step without one; block = every pack before the first tick, no queue (as before P5). budget_ms: in queue mode a second pack is attached in the same tick only while the attaches of this tick used less than this.
cost_note: model: a pack tick costs cost_model_ms (a run is then a pure function of its walk script). measured: the world's own clock, smoothed (ema_shift: 1/2^n per tick).
